metadata.title: On an injectivity lemma in the proof of Tannakian duality

Remark 2.8 mixes a cited fact (Serre) with an open question; kept as remark with the question nested as an open_problem.

nodes.name: Fixed noetherian domain R
nodes.statement: Throughout this work we shall fix a commutative noetherian domain $R$.

nodes.name: Quotient field K
nodes.statement: The quotient field of $R$ will be denoted by $K$.

nodes.name: Module categories mod(A), mod_f(A)
nodes.statement: For an algebra (or more general a ring) $A$ (commutative or not), ${\rm mod}(A)$ denotes the category of left $A$-modules and ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(A)$ denotes the subcategory finitely generated modules.
nodes.statement_short: mod(A) is the category of left A-modules; mod_f(A) the finitely generated ones.

nodes.name: Comodule categories comod(C), comod_f(C)
nodes.statement: For a coalgebra $C$ over $R$, ${\rm comod}(C)$ denotes the category of right $C$-comodules, and ${\rm comod}_{\rm f}(C)$ denotes the subcategory of comodules which are {\em finite over $R$}.
nodes.statement_short: comod(C) is the category of right C-comodules; comod_f(C) those finite over R.

nodes.name: Homomorphism of finite dimensional k-algebras f:A->B
nodes.statement: Let $k$ be a field and $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of finite dimensional $k$-algebras.
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma

nodes.name: Induced restriction functor omega (algebras over a field)
nodes.statement: Then $f$ induces a functor $\omega: {\rm mod}_{\rm f}(B)\to{\rm mod}_{\rm f}(A)$ between the categories of finite modules over $A$ and $B$, which is identity on the underlying vector spaces.
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma
differentia: identity on the underlying vector spaces

nodes.name: Surjectivity criterion for algebra homomorphisms
nodes.statement: A homomorphism $f$ given as above is surjective if and only if the induced functor $\omega$ is full and has the property: for any $B$-module $X$ and any $A$-submodule $Y$ of $\omega(X)$, there exists a $B$-submodule $X'$ of $X$ such that $\omega(X')=Y$. In other words $f$ is surjective if and only if ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(B)$, by means of $f$, is a full (abelian) subcategory of ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(A)$, closed under taking submodules.
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma
conclusions: is surjective if and only if the induced functor $\omega$ is full and has the property: for any $B$-module $X$ and any $A$-submodule $Y$ of $\omega(X)$, there exists a $B$-submodule $X'$ of $X$ such that $\omega(X')=Y$
$f$ is surjective if and only if ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(B)$, by means of $f$, is a full (abelian) subcategory of ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(A)$, closed under taking submodules
equivalent_conditions: the induced functor $\omega$ is full and has the property: for any $B$-module $X$ and any $A$-submodule $Y$ of $\omega(X)$, there exists a $B$-submodule $X'$ of $X$ such that $\omega(X')=Y$
nodes.statement_short: f:A->B is surjective iff mod_f(B) is a full subcategory of mod_f(A) closed under submodules.
nodes.label: lem1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1.1
nodes.statement: If $f$ is surjective then obviously $\omega$ has the claimed properties. We prove the converse statement. Thus for any $B$-module $X$ and any submodule $Y$ of $X$, considered as modules over $A$, we know that $Y$ is also stable under the action of $B$ (obtained by restricting the action of $B$ on $X$). Assume the contrary that $f$ is not surjective, i.e., $B_0:={\rm im} (f)$ is a strict subalgebra of $B$. Then $B_0\subset B$ is an inclusion of $A$-modules, $B$ it self is a $B$-module, but $B_0$ is not stable under the action of $B$ as it contains the unit of $B$. A contradiction.
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: the image $B_0$ of $f$ is an $A$-submodule of $B$ containing the unit, not stable under $B$.

nodes.name: Easy direction and reformulation
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma
nodes.statement: If $f$ is surjective then obviously $\omega$ has the claimed properties. We prove the converse statement. Thus for any $B$-module $X$ and any submodule $Y$ of $X$, considered as modules over $A$, we know that $Y$ is also stable under the action of $B$ (obtained by restricting the action of $B$ on $X$).
nodes.statement_short: Easy direction; for the converse, A-submodules are B-stable.

nodes.name: Assume f not surjective
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma
nodes.statement: Assume the contrary that $f$ is not surjective, i.e., $B_0:={\rm im} (f)$ is a strict subalgebra of $B$.
nodes.statement_short: Suppose the image $B_0$ is a strict subalgebra.

nodes.name: B_0 not B-stable, contradiction
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma
nodes.statement: Then $B_0\subset B$ is an inclusion of $A$-modules, $B$ it self is a $B$-module, but $B_0$ is not stable under the action of $B$ as it contains the unit of $B$. A contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: $B_0\subset B$ is an A-submodule not B-stable: contradiction.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1.2 by duality
nodes.statement: By duality we have the following result for comodules.
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma
nodes.statement_short: Dualize Lemma 1.1 (coalgebra C ↔ dual algebra).

nodes.name: Injectivity lemma
nodes.statement: Let $f:C\to D$ be a homomorphism of finite dimensional $k$-coalgebras. Then the category ${\rm comod}_{\rm f}(C)$, considered by means of $f$ as a subcategory of ${\rm comod}_{\rm f}(D)$, is full and closed under taking subobjects if and only if $f$ is injective.
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma
nodes.origin_citation: Saavedra Rivano 1972 (2.6.3(f)); Szamuely Prop. 6.4.4; Hashimoto Lem. 3.6.10
assumptions: $f:C\to D$ be a homomorphism of finite dimensional $k$-coalgebras
conclusions: the category ${\rm comod}_{\rm f}(C)$, considered by means of $f$ as a subcategory of ${\rm comod}_{\rm f}(D)$, is full and closed under taking subobjects if and only if $f$ is injective
equivalent_conditions: the category ${\rm comod}_{\rm f}(C)$, considered by means of $f$ as a subcategory of ${\rm comod}_{\rm f}(D)$, is full and closed under taking subobjects
also_stated_at: The injectivity lemma claims that, under this correspondence, fully faithful exact functors, which preserves subobjects, correspond to injective homomorphisms of coalgebras (see Lemma \ref{lem2} for the precise formulation).
nodes.statement_short: comod_f(C) is a full subcategory of comod_f(D) closed under subobjects iff the coalgebra map f is injective.
nodes.label: lem2

nodes.name: Dropping finite dimensionality in Lemmas 1.1 and 1.2
nodes.statement: In the proof of Lemma \ref{lem1}, there is no need to assume that $A$ is finite dimensional. Therefore, in Lemma \ref{lem2} there is no need to assume that $D$ is finite dimensional. On the other hand, it is known that each coalgebra is the union of its finite dimensional subcoalgebras. Therefore there is no need to impose the dimension condition on $C$ either.
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma
nodes.statement_short: Finite-dimensionality hypotheses in Lemmas 1.1 and 1.2 can be dropped, using that coalgebras are unions of finite dimensional subcoalgebras.
nodes.label: rmk3

nodes.name: R-finite (torsion-free, flat, projective, free) modules
nodes.statement: Modules over such an algebra are automatically $R$-modules, we call such a module $R$-finite (resp. torsion-free, flat, projective, free) if it is finite (resp. torsion-free, flat, projective, free) over $R$.
nodes.statement_short: A module over an R-algebra is called R-finite/torsion-free/flat/... if it is so as an R-module.

nodes.name: Base change notation ( )_S
nodes.statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative algebras. Then the base change $R\to S$ will be denoted by the subscript $( )_S$.
nodes.statement_short: Subscript S denotes base change along R->S.

nodes.name: Base change of modules and maps M_S, f_S
nodes.statement: For instance $M_S:=M\otimes_RS$, $f_S:=f\otimes_RS$ for an $R$-linear map $f$.

nodes.name: Homomorphism of finite torsion-free R-algebras f:A->B
nodes.statement: Let $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of finite, torsion-free $R$-algebras.

nodes.name: Induced functor omega (R-algebras)
nodes.statement: It induces a functor $\omega:{\rm mod}_\text{f}(B)\to {\rm mod}_\text{f}(A)$, which is identity functor on the underlying $R$-modules, therefore it is faithful and exact.

nodes.name: Surjectivity criterion over a noetherian domain
nodes.statement: The map $f$ as above is surjective if and only if ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(B)$ when considered by means of $f$ as a subcategory of ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(A)$ is full and closed under taking subobjects.
conclusions: \label{lem4} is surjective if and only if ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(B)$ when considered by means of $f$ as a subcategory of ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(A)$ is full and closed under taking subobjects
equivalent_conditions: ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(B)$ when considered by means of $f$ as a subcategory of ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(A)$ is full and closed under taking subobjects
nodes.statement_short: For finite torsion-free R-algebras, f is surjective iff mod_f(B) is full in mod_f(A) and closed under subobjects.
nodes.label: lem4

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: Only the ``if'' claim needs verification. Let $\mathfrak m\in R$ be a maximal ideal and let $k(\mathfrak m):=R/\mathfrak m$ be the residue field. Then the full subcategory of ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(A)$ annihilated by $\mathfrak m$ is equivalent to ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(A_{k(\mathfrak m)})$. Note that this subcategory is also closed under taking subobjects. Thus, by assumption, ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(B_{k(\mathfrak m)})$ is a full subcategory of ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(A_{k(\mathfrak m)})$, closed under taking subobjects. Therefore the map $f_{k(\mathfrak m)} :A_{k(\mathfrak m)}\to B_{k(\mathfrak m)}$ is surjective, by means of Lemma \ref{lem1}. This holds for any maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$, hence $(B/f(A))_{k(\mathfrak m)}=0$ for all maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$. According to \cite[Thm~4.8]{Mats}, we conclude that $B/f(A)$ itself is zero.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to residue fields $k(\mathfrak m)$, apply Lemma 1.1 fiberwise, then Nakayama-type result (Matsumura Thm 4.8) gives $B/f(A)=0$.

nodes.name: Reduction to the if direction and residue fields
nodes.statement: Only the ``if'' claim needs verification. Let $\mathfrak m\in R$ be a maximal ideal and let $k(\mathfrak m):=R/\mathfrak m$ be the residue field. Then the full subcategory of ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(A)$ annihilated by $\mathfrak m$ is equivalent to ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(A_{k(\mathfrak m)})$. Note that this subcategory is also closed under taking subobjects.
nodes.statement_short: Fix a maximal ideal; the m-annihilated subcategory is mod_f(A_{k(m)}), closed under subobjects.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 1.1 on fibers
nodes.statement: Thus, by assumption, ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(B_{k(\mathfrak m)})$ is a full subcategory of ${\rm mod}_{\rm f}(A_{k(\mathfrak m)})$, closed under taking subobjects. Therefore the map $f_{k(\mathfrak m)} :A_{k(\mathfrak m)}\to B_{k(\mathfrak m)}$ is surjective, by means of Lemma \ref{lem1}.
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 1.1, $f_{k(\mathfrak m)}$ is surjective.

nodes.name: Conclude B/f(A)=0
nodes.statement: This holds for any maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$, hence $(B/f(A))_{k(\mathfrak m)}=0$ for all maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$. According to \cite[Thm~4.8]{Mats}, we conclude that $B/f(A)$ itself is zero.
nodes.statement_short: All fibers of $B/f(A)$ vanish, so $B/f(A)=0$ by Matsumura.

nodes.name: Alternative proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: Lemma \ref{lem4} can also be proved in the same way as Lemma \ref{lem1}. We prefer to present the above proof as its main idea (using base change) will be exploited further.

nodes.name: Saturated submodule
nodes.statement: An $A$-submodule $N$ of $M$ is said to be {\em saturated} iff $M/N$ is $R$-torsion-free.

nodes.name: Dominant homomorphism
nodes.statement: A homomorphism $f:A\to B$ is said to be {\em dominant} if $f_K :A_K \to B_K$ is surjective, or equivalently $B/f(A)$ is $R$-torsion. Here $K$ denotes the quotient field of $R$.

nodes.name: Dominance and surjectivity via saturated subobjects (algebras)
nodes.statement: Let $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of $R$-torsion free algebras and assume that $B$ is $R$-finite. Let $\omega:{\rm mod}_{\rm f}(B)\to{\rm mod}_{\rm f}(A)$ be the induced functor. Then: \begin{enumerate}\item The image of $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subobjects of $R$-torsion-free objects iff $f$ is dominant. In this case $\omega$ is also closed under taking saturated submodules of any modules and its restriction to the subcategory of $R$-torsion-free modules is full. \item The image of $\omega$ is closed under taking subobjects of $R$-torsion-free objects iff $f$ is surjective. (In this case $\omega$ is also obviously full.) \end{enumerate}
assumptions: $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of $R$-torsion free algebras
conclusions: The image of $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subobjects of $R$-torsion-free objects iff $f$ is dominant
$\omega$ is also closed under taking saturated submodules of any modules and its restriction to the subcategory of $R$-torsion-free modules is full
The image of $\omega$ is closed under taking subobjects of $R$-torsion-free objects iff $f$ is surjective
The image of $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subobjects of $R$-torsion-free objects iff $f$ is dominant
$\omega$ is also closed under taking saturated submodules of any modules and its restriction to the subcategory of $R$-torsion-free modules is full
The image of $\omega$ is closed under taking subobjects of $R$-torsion-free objects iff $f$ is surjective

nodes.statement_short: f dominant iff image of omega closed under saturated subobjects of torsion-free objects; f surjective iff closed under all such subobjects.
nodes.label: prop5

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.2
nodes.statement: (1). Assume that $\omega$ has the required property. We show that $f$ is dominant, i.e. $f_K$ is surjective. It suffices to show that the functor $\omega_K:{\rm mod}(B_K)\to {\rm mod}(A_K)$ induced from $f_K$ satisfies the condition of Lemma \ref{lem1}. Let $X$ be a finite $B_K$-module and $Y\subset X$ an $A_K$-submodule. Consider $X$ as a $B$-module, take a $K$-basis of $X$ such that a part of it is a basis of $Y$ and let $M$ be the $B$-submodule generated by this basis, let $N:=M\cap Y$. Then $N_K=Y$ (as it contains a $K$-basis of $Y$). By the diagram below $M/N$ is $R$-torsion-free. $$\xymatrix{0\ar[r]&N\ar[r]\ar@{^(->}[d]& M\ar[r]\ar@{^(->}[d]& M/N\ar[r]\ar@{^(->} [d]&0\\ 0\ar[r]& Y\ar[r]& X\ar[r]&X/Y\ar[r]&0.}$$ Thus $N$ is a saturated submodule of $M$, hence, by assumption, $N$ is stable under $B$, consequently $Y=N_K$ is stable under $B_K$. Conversely, assume that $f$ is dominant, i.e., $f_K$ is surjective. Then $\omega_K$ is fully faithful and closed under taking submodules. Let $M$ be an $R$-torsion-free $B$-module, $N\subset M$ be a saturated $A$-submodule. Then $M/N$ is also $R$-torsion-free, hence $N=M\cap N_K$. Now $N_K$ is stable under $B_K$ and $M$ is stable under $B$, showing that $N$ is stable under $B$. Let $\varphi:M\to N$ be an $A$-linear map, where $M,N$ are both $R$-torsion-free then $\varphi$ is determined by $\varphi_K:M_K\to N_K$. Since $f_K$ is surjective, we know that $\varphi_K$ is $A_K$-linear, hence also $B_K$-linear, implying that $f$ is $B$-linear. Thus $\omega$ restricted to $R$-torsion free modules is full. Let now $M$ be a finite $A$-module, $N$ be a finite $B$-module and $\varphi:M\to N$ be an injective $A$-linear map with $M/\varphi(N)$ being $R$-torsion free. Consider a finite free $B$-linear cover $\psi:N'\to N$. Let $\varphi':M'\to N'$ be the pull-back of $\varphi$ along $\psi$ (as $A$-modules). $$\xymatrix{M'\ar@{->>}[d]_{\psi'}\ar@{^(->}[r]^{\varphi'}&N'\ar@{->>}[d]^\psi\\ M\ar@{^(->}[r]_\varphi &N.}$$ Then $\varphi'$ is injective and $\psi':M'\to M$ is surjective, moreover $N'/\varphi'(M')\cong N/\varphi(N)$ hence is $R$-torsion free. Consequently, $M'$ is $B$-stable and, since $\varphi\psi'=\psi\varphi'$ is $B$-linear, there is a $B$-action on $M$ making $\varphi$ $B$-linear. (2). According to the proof of Lemma \ref{lem4}, it suffices to show that for any maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$, the image of $\omega_{k(\mathfrak m)}$ is closed under taking submodules. Let $V$ be a $B_{k(\mathfrak m)}$-module and let $\varphi:U\to V$ be an inclusion of $A_{k(\mathfrak m)}$-modules. Represent $V$ as a quotient of some (free) $B$-modules $M$, then $U$ will be a quotient of some $A$-submodule $N$ of $M$. We have $N$ is $R$-torsion-free, hence, by assumption, $N$ is stable under $B$, so that $U$ must be $B_{k(\mathfrak m)}$-stable.
nodes.statement_short: (1) Pass to the generic fiber and use Lemma 1.1 with saturated lattices; converse via $N=M\cap N_K$ and pull-back along a free cover. (2) Reduce to residue fields as in Lemma 2.1.

nodes.name: Part (1)
nodes.statement: (1). Assume that $\omega$ has the required property. We show that $f$ is dominant, i.e. $f_K$ is surjective. It suffices to show that the functor $\omega_K:{\rm mod}(B_K)\to {\rm mod}(A_K)$ induced from $f_K$ satisfies the condition of Lemma \ref{lem1}. Let $X$ be a finite $B_K$-module and $Y\subset X$ an $A_K$-submodule. Consider $X$ as a $B$-module, take a $K$-basis of $X$ such that a part of it is a basis of $Y$ and let $M$ be the $B$-submodule generated by this basis, let $N:=M\cap Y$. Then $N_K=Y$ (as it contains a $K$-basis of $Y$). By the diagram below $M/N$ is $R$-torsion-free. $$\xymatrix{0\ar[r]&N\ar[r]\ar@{^(->}[d]& M\ar[r]\ar@{^(->}[d]& M/N\ar[r]\ar@{^(->} [d]&0\\ 0\ar[r]& Y\ar[r]& X\ar[r]&X/Y\ar[r]&0.}$$ Thus $N$ is a saturated submodule of $M$, hence, by assumption, $N$ is stable under $B$, consequently $Y=N_K$ is stable under $B_K$. Conversely, assume that $f$ is dominant, i.e., $f_K$ is surjective. Then $\omega_K$ is fully faithful and closed under taking submodules. Let $M$ be an $R$-torsion-free $B$-module, $N\subset M$ be a saturated $A$-submodule. Then $M/N$ is also $R$-torsion-free, hence $N=M\cap N_K$. Now $N_K$ is stable under $B_K$ and $M$ is stable under $B$, showing that $N$ is stable under $B$. Let $\varphi:M\to N$ be an $A$-linear map, where $M,N$ are both $R$-torsion-free then $\varphi$ is determined by $\varphi_K:M_K\to N_K$. Since $f_K$ is surjective, we know that $\varphi_K$ is $A_K$-linear, hence also $B_K$-linear, implying that $f$ is $B$-linear. Thus $\omega$ restricted to $R$-torsion free modules is full. Let now $M$ be a finite $A$-module, $N$ be a finite $B$-module and $\varphi:M\to N$ be an injective $A$-linear map with $M/\varphi(N)$ being $R$-torsion free. Consider a finite free $B$-linear cover $\psi:N'\to N$. Let $\varphi':M'\to N'$ be the pull-back of $\varphi$ along $\psi$ (as $A$-modules). $$\xymatrix{M'\ar@{->>}[d]_{\psi'}\ar@{^(->}[r]^{\varphi'}&N'\ar@{->>}[d]^\psi\\ M\ar@{^(->}[r]_\varphi &N.}$$ Then $\varphi'$ is injective and $\psi':M'\to M$ is surjective, moreover $N'/\varphi'(M')\cong N/\varphi(N)$ hence is $R$-torsion free. Consequently, $M'$ is $B$-stable and, since $\varphi\psi'=\psi\varphi'$ is $B$-linear, there is a $B$-action on $M$ making $\varphi$ $B$-linear.
nodes.statement_short: Prove part (1): both directions and the extra closure/fullness.

nodes.name: Saturated closure implies dominant
nodes.statement: (1). Assume that $\omega$ has the required property. We show that $f$ is dominant, i.e. $f_K$ is surjective. It suffices to show that the functor $\omega_K:{\rm mod}(B_K)\to {\rm mod}(A_K)$ induced from $f_K$ satisfies the condition of Lemma \ref{lem1}. Let $X$ be a finite $B_K$-module and $Y\subset X$ an $A_K$-submodule. Consider $X$ as a $B$-module, take a $K$-basis of $X$ such that a part of it is a basis of $Y$ and let $M$ be the $B$-submodule generated by this basis, let $N:=M\cap Y$. Then $N_K=Y$ (as it contains a $K$-basis of $Y$). By the diagram below $M/N$ is $R$-torsion-free. $$\xymatrix{0\ar[r]&N\ar[r]\ar@{^(->}[d]& M\ar[r]\ar@{^(->}[d]& M/N\ar[r]\ar@{^(->} [d]&0\\ 0\ar[r]& Y\ar[r]& X\ar[r]&X/Y\ar[r]&0.}$$ Thus $N$ is a saturated submodule of $M$, hence, by assumption, $N$ is stable under $B$, consequently $Y=N_K$ is stable under $B_K$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume the closure property; show f dominant.

nodes.name: Assume the property
nodes.statement: (1). Assume that $\omega$ has the required property.
nodes.statement_short: Assume omega has the property.

nodes.name: Claim: f_K surjective
nodes.statement: We show that $f$ is dominant, i.e. $f_K$ is surjective. It suffices to show that the functor $\omega_K:{\rm mod}(B_K)\to {\rm mod}(A_K)$ induced from $f_K$ satisfies the condition of Lemma \ref{lem1}. Let $X$ be a finite $B_K$-module and $Y\subset X$ an $A_K$-submodule. Consider $X$ as a $B$-module, take a $K$-basis of $X$ such that a part of it is a basis of $Y$ and let $M$ be the $B$-submodule generated by this basis, let $N:=M\cap Y$. Then $N_K=Y$ (as it contains a $K$-basis of $Y$). By the diagram below $M/N$ is $R$-torsion-free. $$\xymatrix{0\ar[r]&N\ar[r]\ar@{^(->}[d]& M\ar[r]\ar@{^(->}[d]& M/N\ar[r]\ar@{^(->} [d]&0\\ 0\ar[r]& Y\ar[r]& X\ar[r]&X/Y\ar[r]&0.}$$ Thus $N$ is a saturated submodule of $M$, hence, by assumption, $N$ is stable under $B$, consequently $Y=N_K$ is stable under $B_K$.
nodes.statement_short: Claim f_K surjective, via Lemma 1.1 for omega_K.

nodes.name: Reduce to Lemma 1.1 for omega_K
nodes.statement: We show that $f$ is dominant, i.e. $f_K$ is surjective. It suffices to show that the functor $\omega_K:{\rm mod}(B_K)\to {\rm mod}(A_K)$ induced from $f_K$ satisfies the condition of Lemma \ref{lem1}.
nodes.statement_short: Suffices: omega_K satisfies Lemma 1.1's condition.

nodes.name: Construct lattice M and N
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a finite $B_K$-module and $Y\subset X$ an $A_K$-submodule. Consider $X$ as a $B$-module, take a $K$-basis of $X$ such that a part of it is a basis of $Y$ and let $M$ be the $B$-submodule generated by this basis, let $N:=M\cap Y$. Then $N_K=Y$ (as it contains a $K$-basis of $Y$).
nodes.statement_short: Choose a basis adapted to Y, let M be the B-span and N=M∩Y with N_K=Y.

nodes.name: N saturated hence Y stable
nodes.statement: By the diagram below $M/N$ is $R$-torsion-free. $$\xymatrix{0\ar[r]&N\ar[r]\ar@{^(->}[d]& M\ar[r]\ar@{^(->}[d]& M/N\ar[r]\ar@{^(->} [d]&0\\ 0\ar[r]& Y\ar[r]& X\ar[r]&X/Y\ar[r]&0.}$$ Thus $N$ is a saturated submodule of $M$, hence, by assumption, $N$ is stable under $B$, consequently $Y=N_K$ is stable under $B_K$.
nodes.statement_short: M/N torsion-free so N saturated, B-stable; hence Y is B_K-stable.

nodes.name: Dominant implies saturated closure
nodes.statement: Conversely, assume that $f$ is dominant, i.e., $f_K$ is surjective. Then $\omega_K$ is fully faithful and closed under taking submodules. Let $M$ be an $R$-torsion-free $B$-module, $N\subset M$ be a saturated $A$-submodule. Then $M/N$ is also $R$-torsion-free, hence $N=M\cap N_K$. Now $N_K$ is stable under $B_K$ and $M$ is stable under $B$, showing that $N$ is stable under $B$.
nodes.statement_short: If f_K surjective, saturated A-submodules N=M∩N_K are B-stable.

nodes.name: Fullness on torsion-free modules
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi:M\to N$ be an $A$-linear map, where $M,N$ are both $R$-torsion-free then $\varphi$ is determined by $\varphi_K:M_K\to N_K$. Since $f_K$ is surjective, we know that $\varphi_K$ is $A_K$-linear, hence also $B_K$-linear, implying that $f$ is $B$-linear. Thus $\omega$ restricted to $R$-torsion free modules is full.
nodes.statement_short: A-linear maps of torsion-free modules are determined over K, hence B-linear.

nodes.name: Closure under saturated submodules of any module
nodes.statement: Let now $M$ be a finite $A$-module, $N$ be a finite $B$-module and $\varphi:M\to N$ be an injective $A$-linear map with $M/\varphi(N)$ being $R$-torsion free. Consider a finite free $B$-linear cover $\psi:N'\to N$. Let $\varphi':M'\to N'$ be the pull-back of $\varphi$ along $\psi$ (as $A$-modules). $$\xymatrix{M'\ar@{->>}[d]_{\psi'}\ar@{^(->}[r]^{\varphi'}&N'\ar@{->>}[d]^\psi\\ M\ar@{^(->}[r]_\varphi &N.}$$ Then $\varphi'$ is injective and $\psi':M'\to M$ is surjective, moreover $N'/\varphi'(M')\cong N/\varphi(N)$ hence is $R$-torsion free. Consequently, $M'$ is $B$-stable and, since $\varphi\psi'=\psi\varphi'$ is $B$-linear, there is a $B$-action on $M$ making $\varphi$ $B$-linear.
nodes.statement_short: Pull back along a free cover to reduce to the torsion-free case.

nodes.name: Part (2)
nodes.statement: (2). According to the proof of Lemma \ref{lem4}, it suffices to show that for any maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$, the image of $\omega_{k(\mathfrak m)}$ is closed under taking submodules. Let $V$ be a $B_{k(\mathfrak m)}$-module and let $\varphi:U\to V$ be an inclusion of $A_{k(\mathfrak m)}$-modules. Represent $V$ as a quotient of some (free) $B$-modules $M$, then $U$ will be a quotient of some $A$-submodule $N$ of $M$. We have $N$ is $R$-torsion-free, hence, by assumption, $N$ is stable under $B$, so that $U$ must be $B_{k(\mathfrak m)}$-stable.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to residue fields as in Lemma 2.1 and lift submodules to torsion-free ones.

nodes.name: Comodule categories of flat coalgebras are abelian
nodes.statement: For such coalgebras the comodule categories are abelian, see, e.g. \cite[Lem.~3.3.3]{Ha} or \cite[Thm.~3.13]{BW}. Moreover, the kernel and image of a comodule homomorphism are the same as those of the underlying $R$-module homomorphism.
conclusions: the comodule categories are abelian

nodes.name: Induced restriction functor omega (coalgebras)
nodes.statement: A homomorphism of flat $R$-coalgebras $f:C\to D$ induces the restriction functor $\omega:{\rm comod}(C)\to {\rm comod}(D)$ which is the identity functor on the underlying $R$-module.
differentia: the identity functor on the underlying $R$-module

nodes.name: Pure homomorphism of coalgebras
nodes.statement: We say that a homomorphism of flat $R$-coalgebras $f:C\to D$ is pure if it is a pure homomorphism of $R$-modules. This condition is the same as requiring $D/f(C)$ be $R$-flat.
differentia: it is a pure homomorphism of $R$-modules

nodes.name: Finite flat modules over a noetherian domain are projective
nodes.statement: Note also that over a noetherian domain, finite flat modules are projective.
conclusions: finite flat modules are projective

nodes.name: Duality: injectivity vs dominance/surjectivity of the dual
nodes.statement: Let $C$ be an $R$-finite flat (hence projective) module and $D$ be an $R$-projective module. Then: \begin{enumerate}\item $f$ is injective iff $f^\vee:D^\vee\to C^\vee$ is dominant; \item $f$ is injective and pure iff $f^\vee:D^\vee\to C^\vee$ is surjective, \end{enumerate} where $C^\vee:={\rm Hom}_R(C,R)$.
conclusions: $f$ is injective iff $f^\vee:D^\vee\to C^\vee$ is dominant
$f$ is injective and pure iff $f^\vee:D^\vee\to C^\vee$ is surjective
$f$ is injective iff $f^\vee:D^\vee\to C^\vee$ is dominant
$f$ is injective and pure iff $f^\vee:D^\vee\to C^\vee$ is surjective

nodes.statement_short: For C finite flat and D projective, f injective iff f^∨ dominant; f injective and pure iff f^∨ surjective.
nodes.label: lem6

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement: Embedding $D$ as a direct summand into a free module does not change the properties of $f$ and $f^\vee$, hence we can assume that $D$ is free. Since $C$ is finite, there exists a finite direct summand of $D$ which contains the image of $f$ and we can replace $D$ by this summand, that means we can assume that $D$ is finite. The claims for finite projective modules are obvious. For (1), it involves only the generic fibers. For (2), $f:C\to D$ is pure iff $D/f(C)$ projective, and iff the sequence $0\to C\to D\to D/f(C)\to 0$ is split exact, iff the sequence $0\to (D/f(C))^\vee\to D^\vee\to C^\vee\to 0$ is split exact.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to D finite free, then (1) is a generic-fiber check and (2) follows from split exactness of the dual sequence.

nodes.name: Reduce to D free
nodes.statement: Embedding $D$ as a direct summand into a free module does not change the properties of $f$ and $f^\vee$, hence we can assume that $D$ is free.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG D free.

nodes.name: Reduce to D finite
nodes.statement: Since $C$ is finite, there exists a finite direct summand of $D$ which contains the image of $f$ and we can replace $D$ by this summand, that means we can assume that $D$ is finite.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG D finite.

nodes.name: Part (1) via generic fibers
nodes.statement: The claims for finite projective modules are obvious. For (1), it involves only the generic fibers.
nodes.statement_short: (1) only involves generic fibers.

nodes.name: Part (2) via split exactness
nodes.statement: For (2), $f:C\to D$ is pure iff $D/f(C)$ projective, and iff the sequence $0\to C\to D\to D/f(C)\to 0$ is split exact, iff the sequence $0\to (D/f(C))^\vee\to D^\vee\to C^\vee\to 0$ is split exact.
nodes.statement_short: Purity iff split exactness, which dualizes.

nodes.name: Saturated subcomodule
nodes.statement: A subcomodule $N$ of a $C$-comodule $M$ said to be saturated if $M/N$ is $R$-torsion free.

nodes.name: Injectivity criterion for R-projective coalgebras
nodes.statement: Let $C,D$ be $R$-projective coalgebras. Let $f:C\to D$ be a homomorphism of $R$-coalgebras and $\omega:{\rm comod}_{\rm f}(C)\to{\rm comod}_{\rm f}(D)$ be the induced functor. Assume that $C$ is $R$-finite. Then: \begin{enumerate} \item The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subcomodules of $R$- torsion-free comodules iff $f$ is injective. In this case $\omega$ is also closed under taking saturated subcomodules of any comodules and its restriction to the subcategory of $R$-torsion-free comodules is full. \item The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking subcomodules of $R$-torsion-free comodules iff $f$ is injective and pure. (In this case $\omega$ is also obviously full.) \end{enumerate}
conclusions: The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subcomodules of $R$- torsion-free comodules iff $f$ is injective
In this case $\omega$ is also closed under taking saturated subcomodules of any comodules and its restriction to the subcategory of $R$-torsion-free comodules is full
The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking subcomodules of $R$-torsion-free comodules iff $f$ is injective and pure
The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subcomodules of $R$- torsion-free comodules iff $f$ is injective
In this case $\omega$ is also closed under taking saturated subcomodules of any comodules and its restriction to the subcategory of $R$-torsion-free comodules is full
The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking subcomodules of $R$-torsion-free comodules iff $f$ is injective and pure

nodes.statement_short: For R-projective coalgebras with C finite: f injective iff image closed under saturated subcomodules; injective and pure iff closed under all subcomodules.
nodes.label: prop9

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.4
nodes.statement: Since $D$ is projective, the natural functor ${\rm comod}(D)\to {\rm mod}(D^\vee)$ is fully faithful, exact with image closed under taking subobjects \cite[3.10]{Ha}. Thus the functor, induced from $\omega$, ${\rm mod}(D^\vee)\to {\rm mod}(C^\vee)$ is fully faithful, exact and has image closed under taking subobjects iff $\omega$ is. The claim follows from Proposition \ref{prop5} and Lemma \ref{lem6}.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to dual algebras via comod(D) ⊂ mod(D^∨) and apply Proposition 2.2 and Lemma 2.3.

nodes.name: Comodules as modules over the dual
nodes.statement: Since $D$ is projective, the natural functor ${\rm comod}(D)\to {\rm mod}(D^\vee)$ is fully faithful, exact with image closed under taking subobjects \cite[3.10]{Ha}.
nodes.statement_short: comod(D) embeds fully faithfully in mod(D^∨), closed under subobjects (Hashimoto).

nodes.name: Transfer properties of omega
nodes.statement: Thus the functor, induced from $\omega$, ${\rm mod}(D^\vee)\to {\rm mod}(C^\vee)$ is fully faithful, exact and has image closed under taking subobjects iff $\omega$ is.
nodes.statement_short: The induced functor on dual module categories has the same properties as omega.

nodes.name: Apply Proposition 2.2 and Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement: The claim follows from Proposition \ref{prop5} and Lemma \ref{lem6}.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude by Proposition 2.2 and Lemma 2.3.

nodes.name: Locally finite coalgebra
nodes.statement: We say that a flat $R$-coalgebra $C$ is locally finite if $C$ is the union of its finite $R$-projective pure subcoalgebras $C_\alpha$, $\alpha\in A$.
differentia: $C$ is the union of its finite $R$-projective pure subcoalgebras $C_\alpha$, $\alpha\in A$

nodes.name: IFP (ind-finite projective property)
nodes.statement: This property is called IFP (ind-finite projective property) in \cite{Ha}.

nodes.name: Injectivity criterion for coalgebras with IFP
nodes.statement: Let $C,D$ be projective $R$-coalgebras. Assume that $C$ has IFP, $C=\bigcup C_\alpha$. Let $f:C\to D$ be a homomorphism of $R$-coalgebras. Then $f$ is injective iff the induced functor $\omega:{\rm comod}_{\rm f}(C)\to{\rm comod}_f(D)$ has image closed under taking subobjects. In particular, ${\rm comod}_{\rm f}(C)$ is the union of its full subcategories ${\rm comod}_{\rm f}(C_\alpha)$, which are closed under taking subobjects.
conclusions: $f$ is injective iff the induced functor $\omega:{\rm comod}_{\rm f}(C)\to{\rm comod}_f(D)$ has image closed under taking subobjects
${\rm comod}_{\rm f}(C)$ is the union of its full subcategories ${\rm comod}_{\rm f}(C_\alpha)$, which are closed under taking subobjects
equivalent_conditions: the induced functor $\omega:{\rm comod}_{\rm f}(C)\to{\rm comod}_f(D)$ has image closed under taking subobjects
nodes.statement_short: For projective coalgebras with IFP, f is injective iff comod_f(C) has image closed under subobjects in comod_f(D).

nodes.name: Flat coalgebras with almost no finite pure subcoalgebras exist
nodes.statement: Notice that there exist $R$-flat coalgebras which contains almost no finite pure subcoalgebras, as shown in the examples below.
conclusions: there exist $R$-flat coalgebras which contains almost no finite pure subcoalgebras

nodes.name: Flat Hopf algebras R[T]/(πT^2+T) and R[T]/(πT^2+2T) (dos Santos)
nodes.statement: \rm (1) Assume that $R$ is a Dedekind ring with characteristic equal to 2 and $\pi\neq 0$ is a non-unit in $R$. Consider the algebra $H:=R[T]/(\pi T^2+T)$ with the coalgebra structure given by $$\Delta(T)=T\otimes 1+1\otimes T.$$ Then $H$ is torsion-free, hence flat over $R$. Let $M\subset H$ be a saturated $R$-finite subcomodule of $H$. Then $M$ is free over $R$, more over its rank is at most 2, as $H_K$ has dimension 2 over $K$. If $M$ has rank 2 then $H/M$ is $R$-torsion, contradiction, hence $M$ has rank 1 over $R$. The coaction of $H$ on $M$ is thus given by a group-like element in $H$. On the other hand, the $R$-flatness of $H$ implies $H\otimes H$ is a submodule of $H_K\otimes_KH_K$, hence the coproduct on $H$ is the restriction of the coproduct on $H_K$: $$\xymatrix{H\ar[r]^{\Delta\quad}\ar[d]& H\otimes H\ar[d]\\ H_K\ar[r]_{\Delta\qquad}& H_K\otimes_KH_K.}$$ Consequently, a group-like element of $H$ is a group-like element of $H_K$. But in $H_K$ the unique group-like element is 1. Thus $M$ is a trivial comodule of $H$. (2) Similarly, assume that $R$ is a Dedekind ring, in which 2 is invertible. Consider the algebra $H:=R[T]/(\pi T^2+2T)$ where $\pi\neq 0$ is a non-unit. $H$ is a Hopf algebra with the coaction given by $$\Delta(T)=T\otimes 1+1\otimes T+\pi T\otimes T.$$ Similar discussion shows that there are only two finite saturated subcomodules of $H$, the one generated by 1 and the other generated by the group-like element $1+\pi T$.
nodes.statement_short: Over a Dedekind ring, the flat Hopf algebras R[T]/(πT^2+T) (char 2) and R[T]/(πT^2+2T) have only trivial or two finite saturated subcomodules.
nodes.label: ex2.5

nodes.name: Injectivity criterion for flat coalgebras
nodes.statement: Let $C,D$ be $R$-flat coalgebras and $f:C\to D$ be a homomorphism of $R$-coalgebras. Let $\omega:{\rm comod}(C)\to{\rm comod}(D)$ be the induced functor on comodule categories. Then: \begin{enumerate} \item The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subcomodules of $R$-torsion-free comodules iff $f$ is injective. In this case $\omega$ is also closed under taking saturated subcomodules of any comodules and its restriction to the subcategory of $R$-torsion-free comodules is full. \item The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking subcomodules of any comodules iff $f$ is injective and pure. In this case $\omega$ is full. \end{enumerate}
conclusions: The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subcomodules of $R$-torsion-free comodules iff $f$ is injective
In this case $\omega$ is also closed under taking saturated subcomodules of any comodules and its restriction to the subcategory of $R$-torsion-free comodules is full
The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking subcomodules of any comodules iff $f$ is injective and pure
In this case $\omega$ is full
The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subcomodules of $R$-torsion-free comodules iff $f$ is injective
In this case $\omega$ is also closed under taking saturated subcomodules of any comodules and its restriction to the subcategory of $R$-torsion-free comodules is full
The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking subcomodules of any comodules iff $f$ is injective and pure
In this case $\omega$ is full

nodes.statement_short: For flat coalgebras: f injective iff image of omega closed under saturated subcomodules of torsion-free comodules; injective and pure iff closed under all subcomodules.
nodes.label: prop9b

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.7
nodes.statement: (1) Assume that $\omega$ has the required property. Let $C_0:={\rm ker}(f)$. Then $C/C_0\cong {\rm im}(f)\subset D$ is $R$-torsion-free, hence $C_0$ is a saturated subcomodule of $C$, considered as $D$-comodules (the big left square with curved vertical arrows below is commutative). By assumption, the coaction of $D$ on $C_0$ lifts to a coaction of $C$. That is, there exists a coaction $C_0\to C_0\otimes C$ (the dotted arrow below) making the following diagram commutative: $$\xymatrix{ C_0\ar[r] \ar@{-->}[d]\ar@/_30pt/[dd] &C\ar[d]^\Delta\ar[r]^f\ar@/^30pt/[dd] & D\ar[dd]^\Delta \\ C_0\otimes C\ar[r]\ar[d]^{{\rm id}\otimes f}& C\otimes C\ar[d]^{{\rm id}\otimes f}&\\ C_0\otimes D\ar[r]&C\otimes D\ar[r]_{f\otimes {\rm id}}&D\otimes D.}$$ In particular, the coaction of $C$ on $C_0$ is the restriction of that on $C$ (the upper-left square). That is, for any $c\in C_0$ we have a representation $$\Delta(c)=\sum_{(c)}c_{(1)}\otimes c_{(2)},$$ with $c_{(1)}\in C_0$. On the other hand, as $f$ is a coalgebra homomorphism, we have $\varepsilon\circ f=\varepsilon$. Consequently, $\varepsilon(C_0)=0$. Applying $\varepsilon\otimes{\rm id}$ to the above equation we get $$c=\sum_{(c)}\varepsilon(c_{(1)})\otimes c_{(2)}=0.$$ A contradiction. Thus ${\rm ker}(f)=0$. Conversely, assume that $f:C\to D$ is injective, then the map $f_K:C_K\to D_K$ is also injective, as the base change $R\to K$ is flat. Hence, according to \ref{lem2}, \ref{rmk3}, $\omega_K$ is fully faithful and is closed under taking subcomodules. Thus $\omega$ is full when restricted to $R$-torsion free comodules. Finally we show that the image of $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subcomodules of any comodules. For an $R$-module $M$, let $M^\text{tor}$ denote its torsion part, i.e. those elements of $M$ killed by some non-zero element of $R$. Then we have $$M^\text{tor}={\rm ker}(M\to M\otimes K).$$ Therefore, for any flat $R$-module $P$ we have $$(M^\text{tor}\otimes P)\cong (M\otimes P)^\text{tor}.$$ Since any $R$-linear map preserves the torsion part, we conclude that, if $M$ is a $C$-comodule then $M^\text{tor}$ is a subcomodule. Let now $N\subset M$ be a subcomodule with respect to the action of $D$. If $M/N$ is $R$-torsion free then $M^\text{tor}=N^\text{tor}$ and hence is stable under the coaction of $C$. Hence we can consider the saturated inclusion $N/N^\text{tor}\subset M/M^\text{tor}$, which by assumption shows that $N/N^\text{tor}$ is stable under the coaction of $C$. As $C$ is flat, we conclude that $N$ itself is stable under $C$. (2) Assume that $\omega$ is closed under taking subcomodules of any comodules. Then according to (1), $f$ is injective. Assume $f$ is not pure, then there exists an ideal $I$ of $R$ such that the induced map $R/I\otimes C\to R/I\otimes D$ is not injective. Let $C_0$ be the kernel of this map. Repeat the argument of the proof of (1) we conclude that $C_0$ is stable under the coaction of $D$ but not under the coaction of $C$, a contradiction. Thus $f$ has to be pure. For the converse, assuming that $f:C\to D$ is injective and pure and $N\subset M$ be $R$-modules, then we have the equality of submodules of $M\otimes D$: $$N\otimes D\cap M\otimes C=N\otimes C,$$ where $C$ is considered as an $R$-submodule of $D$ by means of $f$. Hence, if $M$ is a $C$-comodule and $N$ is a $D$-subcomodule of $M$, then, denote by $\delta$ the coaction, we have $$\delta(N)\subset N\otimes D\cap M\otimes C=N\otimes C.$$ That is, $N$ is stable under the coaction of $C$.
nodes.statement_short: (1) The kernel $C_0$ is a saturated D-subcomodule; lifting its coaction to C and applying the counit forces $C_0=0$. Converse via generic fiber and torsion parts; (2) same argument mod an ideal I, converse by purity.

nodes.name: Part (1)

Then $C/C_0\cong {\rm im}(f)\subset D$ is $R$-torsion-free, hence $C_0$ is a saturated subcomodule of $C$, considered as $D$-comodules (the big left square with curved vertical arrows below is commutative). By assumption, the coaction of $D$ on $C_0$ lifts to a coaction of $C$. For an $R$-module $M$, let $M^\text{tor}$ denote its torsion part, i.e. those elements of $M$ killed by some non-zero element of $R$. Then we have $$M^\text{tor}={\rm ker}(M\to M\otimes K).$$ Therefore, for any flat $R$-module $P$ we have $$(M^\text{tor}\otimes P)\cong (M\otimes P)^\text{tor}.$$ Since any $R$-linear map preserves the torsion part, we conclude that, if $M$ is a $C$-comodule then $M^\text{tor}$ is a subcomodule. Hence we can consider the saturated inclusion $N/N^\text{tor}\subset M/M^\text{tor}$, which by assumption shows that $N/N^\text{tor}$ is stable under the coaction of $C$. As $C$ is flat, we conclude that $N$ itself is stable under $C$.
nodes.statement_short: Prove part (1).

nodes.name: Kernel is a saturated subcomodule
nodes.statement: (1) Assume that $\omega$ has the required property. Let $C_0:={\rm ker}(f)$. Then $C/C_0\cong {\rm im}(f)\subset D$ is $R$-torsion-free, hence $C_0$ is a saturated subcomodule of $C$, considered as $D$-comodules (the big left square with curved vertical arrows below is commutative).
nodes.statement_short: Assume the property; C_0=ker f is saturated in C.

nodes.name: Lift coaction on C_0
nodes.statement: By assumption, the coaction of $D$ on $C_0$ lifts to a coaction of $C$. That is, there exists a coaction $C_0\to C_0\otimes C$ (the dotted arrow below) making the following diagram commutative: $$\xymatrix{ C_0\ar[r] \ar@{-->}[d]\ar@/_30pt/[dd] &C\ar[d]^\Delta\ar[r]^f\ar@/^30pt/[dd] & D\ar[dd]^\Delta \\ C_0\otimes C\ar[r]\ar[d]^{{\rm id}\otimes f}& C\otimes C\ar[d]^{{\rm id}\otimes f}&\\ C_0\otimes D\ar[r]&C\otimes D\ar[r]_{f\otimes {\rm id}}&D\otimes D.}$$ In particular, the coaction of $C$ on $C_0$ is the restriction of that on $C$ (the upper-left square). That is, for any $c\in C_0$ we have a representation $$\Delta(c)=\sum_{(c)}c_{(1)}\otimes c_{(2)},$$ with $c_{(1)}\in C_0$.
nodes.statement_short: The D-coaction on C_0 lifts to a C-coaction restricting that of C.

nodes.name: Counit argument kills kernel
nodes.statement: On the other hand, as $f$ is a coalgebra homomorphism, we have $\varepsilon\circ f=\varepsilon$. Consequently, $\varepsilon(C_0)=0$. Applying $\varepsilon\otimes{\rm id}$ to the above equation we get $$c=\sum_{(c)}\varepsilon(c_{(1)})\otimes c_{(2)}=0.$$ A contradiction. Thus ${\rm ker}(f)=0$.

nodes.name: Injective implies fullness on torsion-free
nodes.statement: Conversely, assume that $f:C\to D$ is injective, then the map $f_K:C_K\to D_K$ is also injective, as the base change $R\to K$ is flat. Hence, according to \ref{lem2}, \ref{rmk3}, $\omega_K$ is fully faithful and is closed under taking subcomodules. Thus $\omega$ is full when restricted to $R$-torsion free comodules.
nodes.statement_short: Generic fiber injective; Lemma 1.2 and Remark 1.3 give fullness.

nodes.name: Closure under saturated subcomodules of any comodule
nodes.statement: Finally we show that the image of $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subcomodules of any comodules. For an $R$-module $M$, let $M^\text{tor}$ denote its torsion part, i.e. those elements of $M$ killed by some non-zero element of $R$. Then we have $$M^\text{tor}={\rm ker}(M\to M\otimes K).$$ Therefore, for any flat $R$-module $P$ we have $$(M^\text{tor}\otimes P)\cong (M\otimes P)^\text{tor}.$$ Since any $R$-linear map preserves the torsion part, we conclude that, if $M$ is a $C$-comodule then $M^\text{tor}$ is a subcomodule. Let now $N\subset M$ be a subcomodule with respect to the action of $D$. If $M/N$ is $R$-torsion free then $M^\text{tor}=N^\text{tor}$ and hence is stable under the coaction of $C$. Hence we can consider the saturated inclusion $N/N^\text{tor}\subset M/M^\text{tor}$, which by assumption shows that $N/N^\text{tor}$ is stable under the coaction of $C$. As $C$ is flat, we conclude that $N$ itself is stable under $C$.
nodes.statement_short: Torsion parts are subcomodules; reduce to the torsion-free saturated case.

nodes.name: Part (2)
nodes.statement: (2) Assume that $\omega$ is closed under taking subcomodules of any comodules. Then according to (1), $f$ is injective. Assume $f$ is not pure, then there exists an ideal $I$ of $R$ such that the induced map $R/I\otimes C\to R/I\otimes D$ is not injective. Let $C_0$ be the kernel of this map. Repeat the argument of the proof of (1) we conclude that $C_0$ is stable under the coaction of $D$ but not under the coaction of $C$, a contradiction. Thus $f$ has to be pure. For the converse, assuming that $f:C\to D$ is injective and pure and $N\subset M$ be $R$-modules, then we have the equality of submodules of $M\otimes D$: $$N\otimes D\cap M\otimes C=N\otimes C,$$ where $C$ is considered as an $R$-submodule of $D$ by means of $f$. Hence, if $M$ is a $C$-comodule and $N$ is a $D$-subcomodule of $M$, then, denote by $\delta$ the coaction, we have $$\delta(N)\subset N\otimes D\cap M\otimes C=N\otimes C.$$ That is, $N$ is stable under the coaction of $C$.
nodes.statement_short: Prove part (2).

nodes.name: Closure implies injective
nodes.statement: (2) Assume that $\omega$ is closed under taking subcomodules of any comodules. Then according to (1), $f$ is injective.
nodes.statement_short: By (1), f is injective.

nodes.name: Purity by contradiction
nodes.statement: Assume $f$ is not pure, then there exists an ideal $I$ of $R$ such that the induced map $R/I\otimes C\to R/I\otimes D$ is not injective. Let $C_0$ be the kernel of this map. Repeat the argument of the proof of (1) we conclude that $C_0$ is stable under the coaction of $D$ but not under the coaction of $C$, a contradiction. Thus $f$ has to be pure.
nodes.statement_short: If not pure, the kernel mod I gives a D-stable non-C-stable subcomodule.

nodes.name: Injective pure implies closure
nodes.statement: For the converse, assuming that $f:C\to D$ is injective and pure and $N\subset M$ be $R$-modules, then we have the equality of submodules of $M\otimes D$: $$N\otimes D\cap M\otimes C=N\otimes C,$$ where $C$ is considered as an $R$-submodule of $D$ by means of $f$. Hence, if $M$ is a $C$-comodule and $N$ is a $D$-subcomodule of $M$, then, denote by $\delta$ the coaction, we have $$\delta(N)\subset N\otimes D\cap M\otimes C=N\otimes C.$$ That is, $N$ is stable under the coaction of $C$.
nodes.statement_short: Purity gives N⊗D ∩ M⊗C = N⊗C, so D-subcomodules are C-stable.

nodes.name: Serre: comodules are unions of R-finite subcomodules
nodes.statement: According to Serre \cite[Prop.~2]{Se}, any object in ${\rm comod}(C)$ is the union of its $R$-finite subcomodules (but generally not saturated). I don't know if one can prove Propsition \ref{prop9b} with ${\rm comod}(C)$, ${\rm comod}(D)$ replaced by ${\rm comod}_f(C)$, ${\rm comod}_f(D)$, respectively.

nodes.name: Proposition 2.7 for finite comodule categories
nodes.statement: I don't know if one can prove Propsition \ref{prop9b} with ${\rm comod}(C)$, ${\rm comod}(D)$ replaced by ${\rm comod}_f(C)$, ${\rm comod}_f(D)$, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Does Proposition 2.7 hold with comod replaced by comod_f?
